tasks.title: Parsing arguments
tasks.statement: Write a function parse_cli(argv): use argparse to parse a list of command-line arguments: a positional text, an optional --count (an integer, 1 by default) and a --upper flag. Return the tuple (text, count, upper).
tasks.hint: p.add_argument('text'); p.add_argument('--count', type=int, default=1); p.add_argument('--upper', action='store_true').

tasks.title: A summing utility
tasks.statement: Write a function main(argv): the arguments in argv are numbers (argparse, nargs='*', type=int). If there are no numbers, print "no numbers" to stderr and return 1; otherwise print the sum and return 0.
tasks.hint: p = argparse.ArgumentParser(); p.add_argument('nums', nargs='*', type=int); args = p.parse_args(argv).

tasks.title: A setting from the environment
tasks.statement: Write a function get_port(): the value of the environment variable PORT as an integer; if the variable is missing, 8000.

tasks.title: Your own logger
tasks.statement: Write a function make_logger(stream): a logger named "app" that writes messages of level INFO and above to the given stream in the format "LEVEL: message" (turn propagate off).

tasks.title: Running a process
tasks.statement: Write a function run_python(code): it runs a child interpreter (sys.executable) with the code code and returns a tuple (return code, output stripped at the edges). Use subprocess.run, capture_output and text.
tasks.hint: r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-c', code], capture_output=True, text=True); return r.returncode, r.stdout.strip().

tasks.title: A process with a timeout
tasks.statement: Write a function run_limited(code, seconds): it runs the code in a child interpreter; if it does not finish within seconds seconds, return the string "timeout", otherwise return its output stripped at the edges.
tasks.hint: try: subprocess.run(..., timeout=seconds) / except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: return "timeout".

tasks.title: Lines from a stream
tasks.statement: Write a function count_lines(stream): how many non-empty lines (after strip) the file object stream contains. Work with the stream the way you would with standard input: iterate over it in a loop.
tasks.hint: n = 0; for line in stream: if line.strip(): n += 1.
